title: Getting a licence without stalling the shop
target: How to add a product line in TCG Card Shop Simulator without wasting money: it covers the level requirement a licence asks for, the difference between an unlocked licence and an active one, and the unlock cost that comes on top.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is open and running
Enough money for the licence and the unlock
A shop level to look at before you commit

steps.do: Check the level requirement before you look at the price.
steps.because: a licence asks for a shop level as well as money, and the screen keeps a requirement line apart from the price (licenseShopLevelRequired, m_LevelRequirementText)

steps.do: Buy the licence as an item rather than treating it as a switch you flip.
steps.because: a licence is an item in the game, listed in its own tab with an indicator for a purchase (LicenseItem, LicensesTab, PurchasedLicenseIndicator)

steps.do: Budget the unlock separately from the licence.
steps.because: unlocking has a cost of its own, and shelves carry an unlock cost multiplier on top (m_UnlockCostText, m_ShelfUnlockCostMultiplier)

steps.do: After buying, check whether the licence is unlocked or actually active.
steps.because: the game keeps the unlocked licences apart from the ones currently active (unlockedLicenses, activeLicenses)

steps.do: If a line still does not appear, look for a disabled licence rather than buying it again.
steps.because: a set of licence numbers can be disabled, which is how a shop can hold a licence without its goods being on sale (disabledLicenseIDs)

steps.do: Do not assume a product will show up because it exists in the game.
steps.because: an item can stay hidden until it is unlocked (isHideItemUntilUnlocked)

steps.do: Expect the purchase to be checked rather than simply granted.
steps.because: the store side keeps a handle and a result the game examines before a licence is acquired (storeLicenseHandle, storeCanAcquireLicenseResult)

steps.do: Plan the order of licences rather than buying whatever is affordable.
steps.because: the licence lists can be sorted by level in either direction, so what is cheap is not the same as what is next (LicenseLevelLowToHigh, LicenseLevelHighToLow)

commonMistakes: Saving for a licence and forgetting the unlock cost on top of it.
Assuming a bought licence is active when it is only unlocked.
Buying a second licence for a line that has been disabled.
Sorting the licence list by price when the requirement is a shop level.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
